recipes.title: Air Fryer Korean Chicken Popcorn

ingredients.name: chicken thighs, boneless skinless, cut into 5cm cubes
green onion stalks, thinly sliced (optional topping)

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Mix the chicken with white pepper, ginger-garlic paste, soy sauce and rice vinegar. Cover and refrigerate at least 30 minutes.

steps.title: Toast the panko
steps.text: Put the panko in a DRY pan over medium-low heat. Stir continuously for 4-5 minutes until pale sand colour, not golden. Tip onto a cold plate immediately. Alternative: air fry at 160°C for 3-4 minutes, shaking every minute.

steps.title: Set up the coating
steps.text: Once cooled, mix the panko with cornflour, garlic powder and a pinch of salt. Beat the egg in a separate bowl.

steps.title: Bread the chicken
steps.text: Dip each piece in egg, then press firmly into the panko mix. Press hard — panko needs pressure to stick.

steps.title: Preheat
steps.text: Run the air fryer empty at 190°C for 3-4 minutes.

steps.title: First cook
steps.text: Single layer with gaps — cook in batches if needed. Spray with half the oil. Cook at 190°C for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Flip and finish
steps.text: Flip, spray with the rest of the oil, cook 5-7 more minutes until deep golden and 74°C inside.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Top with green onions. Serve with garlic yogurt dip.

recipes.notes: Macros exclude the optional wasabi-soy sauce (+~25 kcal per serving): ½ tbsp brown sugar, 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp rice vinegar, 2 tbsp water, ½ tbsp lemon juice, and ½ tbsp wasabi or 1 tbsp gochujang. With chicken breast instead of thighs: ~470 kcal and ~57g protein per serving. Near-zero fibre — pair it with something green.

recipes.title: Garlic-Herb Air-Fried Potato Wedges

ingredients.name: dried oregano or mixed herbs (half before, half after)

steps.title: Cut
steps.text: Cut into even wedges, about 2cm at the thickest point. Even size matters more than shape.

steps.title: Soak
steps.text: Soak in cold water for 30 minutes to pull out surface starch. Drain and dry completely.

steps.title: Parboil
steps.text: Boil in salted water for 6 minutes until a knife meets slight resistance. Drain and steam-dry in the colander for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Shake the colander to rough up the surfaces. Toss with cornflour, oil, garlic powder, onion powder, pepper, salt and half the oregano.

steps.title: First cook
steps.text: Preheat the air fryer to 200°C for 3 minutes. Single layer with gaps. Cook 12 minutes.

steps.title: Shake and finish
steps.text: Shake or flip, then cook 6-8 more minutes until deep golden.

steps.title: Finish with herbs
steps.text: Toss straight away with the rest of the oregano, the thyme and a pinch of salt.

recipes.notes: Already parboiled? Pat dry and start at 'Season'. No chilli by design — a pinch of smoked paprika adds colour without heat. Macros are for 200g raw potato per serving; 100g of finished wedges is ~135 kcal.

recipes.title: Air-Fried Spiced Panko Chicken

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Mix curd, lemon, chilli powder, garam masala, garlic powder, pepper and salt. Coat the chicken and refrigerate at least 30 minutes.

steps.title: Toast the panko
steps.text: Dry pan, medium-low heat, stir continuously 4-5 minutes to pale sand colour. Tip onto a cold plate.

steps.title: Set up the coating
steps.text: Mix cooled panko with cornflour and a pinch of salt. Beat the egg and whites together.

steps.title: Bread
steps.text: Egg first, then press firmly into the panko.

steps.title: Preheat
steps.text: Air fryer at 190°C for 3-4 minutes.

steps.title: First cook
steps.text: Single layer, spray with half the oil, 10 minutes at 190°C.

steps.title: Flip and finish
steps.text: Flip, spray, 5-7 more minutes until golden and 74°C inside.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Rest 2-3 minutes so the crust firms up.

recipes.notes: With thighs: ~440 kcal per serving and more forgiving if you overshoot the timing. Full plate with 200g garlic-herb wedges: ~590 kcal, 50g protein.

recipes.title: Bihari Village Chicken

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Mix the chicken with curd, half the turmeric, half the chilli powder, ginger-garlic paste and 1 tsp salt. Rest 30 minutes.

steps.title: Smoke the mustard oil
steps.text: Heat the oil until it just starts to smoke, lower the heat and let it settle for 30 seconds. Skipping this makes the curry bitter.

steps.title: Bloom whole spices
steps.text: Add bay leaf, cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, cumin seeds and dried chillies. Fry 30-40 seconds.

steps.title: Brown the onions
steps.text: Cook the onions on medium, stirring often, 12-15 minutes (15-18 in a handi) until deep golden brown. Add green chillies for the last 2 minutes. This stage makes the dish.

steps.title: Cook the masala
steps.text: Add tomatoes and the remaining turmeric, chilli, coriander and cumin powder. Cook 6-8 minutes until oil separates at the edges.

steps.title: Bhuno the chicken
steps.text: Add the chicken and remaining salt. Fry on high 8-10 minutes, scraping the pan sides back in, until the masala clings.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Add the hot water, boil, then cover and simmer on low 20-25 minutes. Country chicken needs 40-45.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Sprinkle garam masala, reduce uncovered 2-3 minutes. Rest 10 minutes, then add coriander.

recipes.notes: Chilli powder is set to 1 tsp — your first batch with 2 tsp came out too hot. If it's still too spicy, whisk 3-4 tbsp curd in off the heat. Per 100g finished: ~167 kcal, 16g protein. Cook it in a kadhai or big handi, not a pressure cooker.

recipes.title: Iffa Chicken (High-Protein Creamy Chicken)

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Mix curd, ginger-garlic paste, chilli powder, turmeric, coriander, pepper, garam masala, vinegar and salt. Coat the chicken. At least 1 hour, overnight is better.

steps.title: Make the white sauce
steps.text: Blend egg whites, cheese, skim milk, vinegar, garlic, a pinch of salt and the sugar until smooth and slightly tangy.

steps.title: Sear
steps.text: Spray a nonstick pan with oil. Cook the chicken on medium-high 4-5 minutes per side until golden.

steps.title: Cook through
steps.text: Lower the heat, cover, and cook 4-5 minutes until the masala thickens.

steps.title: Add the sauce
steps.text: Pour the white sauce over, cover and cook on low 2-3 minutes.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Garnish with coriander.

recipes.notes: The best protein-per-calorie ratio of your curries — the blended egg-white-and-cheese sauce replaces cream. With breast: ~275 kcal, 45g protein per serving; the sauce keeps breast moist here. No fibre — serve with vegetables.

recipes.title: Chicken Sukka (Lighter Version)

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Mix the chicken with turmeric, oil and salt. Rest 15-20 minutes.

steps.title: Make the masala
steps.text: Lightly roast coriander, cumin, fenugreek, pepper, cinnamon, cloves, chillies, garlic, ginger and curry leaves with a few drops of oil. Grind smooth with a splash of water.

steps.title: Roast the coconut
steps.text: In the same pan, dry-roast the coconut on high until lightly golden. Stir constantly — it burns fast.

steps.title: Onions
steps.text: Heat ghee, sauté onions 3 minutes, add curry leaves for 2 more, then the salt, and cook until golden brown.

steps.title: Sear the chicken
steps.text: Add the chicken and cook on high 5-7 minutes.

steps.title: Add masala and coconut
steps.text: Stir in the masala paste, cook 5 minutes, then mix in the roasted coconut.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Add the water, cover and cook on medium 15 minutes until tender.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Stir in tamarind pulp and a few fresh curry leaves.

recipes.notes: Lightened from the Instagram original (1 cup coconut, 2 tbsp ghee ≈ 495 kcal per serving). Coconut and ghee are where the calories hide in this dish — resist adding them back.

recipes.title: Homemade Kimchi

ingredients.name: coarse sea salt or rock salt (not iodised)

steps.title: Salt the cabbage
steps.text: Quarter lengthwise, chop into 4-5cm pieces, rinse, then layer with the salt in a big bowl.

steps.title: Wilt
steps.text: Leave 2 hours, turning every 30 minutes, until a leaf bends without snapping.

steps.title: Rinse and drain
steps.text: Rinse 3 times in cold water, then drain 20 minutes. Squeeze gently.

steps.title: Flour paste
steps.text: Whisk flour into the water, cook on medium 3-4 minutes to a thin porridge. Cool completely.

steps.title: Seasoning
steps.text: Mix the cooled paste with ginger-garlic paste, gochugaru, sugar and fish sauce.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Wearing gloves, massage the seasoning into the cabbage, radish and spring onions.

steps.title: Pack
steps.text: Press tightly into a clean glass jar so the brine rises above the vegetables. Leave 3-4cm headspace.

steps.title: Ferment
steps.text: Room temperature for about 1 day in Bengaluru, pressing down daily. Bubbling and sour smell means it's ready.

steps.title: Refrigerate
steps.text: Keeps 2-3 months. Best after a week.

recipes.notes: Gochugaru can't be swapped for Indian chilli powder — it turns harsh and bitter. Always serve with a clean spoon. Discard if it smells rotten rather than sour, or grows fuzzy mould. One serving is about 80g.

recipes.title: Standard Breakfast (Overnight Oats)

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Stir oats, chia and whey into the almond milk until there are no lumps.

steps.title: Add the rest
steps.text: Stir in yogurt and honey. Top with blueberries.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Refrigerate overnight, at least 6 hours.

recipes.notes: Macros exclude what you usually have alongside: 2 boiled eggs + 100g egg whites (~208 kcal, 24g protein) and the pre-workout banana (~105 kcal). Honey is most of the sugar — halving it saves ~8g sugar.

recipes.title: Garlic Greek Yogurt Dip

steps.title: Whisk
steps.text: Whisk everything together until smooth.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Rest 10 minutes so the garlic flavour develops.

recipes.notes: Spicy version: add 1 tsp gochujang or sriracha (+10 kcal). A fraction of mayo's calories, with protein instead of fat.

recipes.title: Mint Curd Chutney

steps.title: Blitz
steps.text: Blend mint, coriander, chilli and lemon with 1 tbsp water to a paste.

steps.title: Mix
steps.text: Whisk the paste into the curd with cumin and salt.

recipes.notes: Goes with anything tandoori.

recipes.title: Air Fryer Tandoori Chicken Tikka

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Mix everything except the onion and capsicum, coat the chicken, and marinate at least 2 hours — overnight is better.

steps.title: Add the vegetables
steps.text: Toss the onion and capsicum into the marinade for the last 10 minutes.

steps.title: Preheat
steps.text: Air fryer at 200°C for 3 minutes.

steps.title: First cook
steps.text: Chicken and vegetables in a single layer, 10 minutes.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Flip and cook 6-8 minutes until the edges char and the inside hits 74°C.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Sprinkle chaat masala and squeeze lemon over.

recipes.notes: One of the best protein-per-calorie options here. Hung curd matters: strain regular curd in a muslin cloth for 2 hours — thin curd makes the tikka soggy. Makes a great wrap filling.

recipes.title: Garlic Pepper Prawns

steps.title: Season
steps.text: Toss the prawns with turmeric, half the pepper and the salt. Rest 10 minutes.

steps.title: Garlic
steps.text: Heat oil and butter on medium. Fry garlic and curry leaves about 1 minute until pale gold — not brown.

steps.title: Sear
steps.text: Turn heat to high, add prawns in a single layer, 2 minutes per side. They're done when they curl into a C; an O means overcooked.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Add the rest of the pepper, chilli flakes, lemon and coriander. Serve immediately.

recipes.notes: Air fryer version: 200°C for 6-7 minutes, then toss in the garlic butter. Prawns overcook fast — take them off a touch early.

recipes.title: Air Fryer Fish Tikka

steps.title: Prep the fish
steps.text: Pat the fish dry, rub with lemon and salt, rest 10 minutes.

steps.title: Roast the besan
steps.text: Dry-roast the besan 1 minute until nutty.

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Mix besan with the curd, spices and oil. Coat the fish gently and rest 30 minutes.

steps.title: Preheat
steps.text: Air fryer at 200°C. Line the basket with lightly oiled foil or parchment — fish sticks.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: 8 minutes, turn gently once, then 4-5 more until it flakes.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Chaat masala and a squeeze of lemon.

recipes.notes: Flip only once — fish is delicate. Basa is the leanest protein you regularly eat.

recipes.title: Chicken Keema Matar

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat oil, add cumin seeds and bay leaf.

steps.title: Onions
steps.text: Cook onions 8-10 minutes until golden.

steps.title: Aromatics
steps.text: Add ginger-garlic paste and green chillies, 1 minute.

steps.title: Masala
steps.text: Add tomatoes and all powders except garam masala. Cook 5-6 minutes until oil separates.

steps.title: Keema
steps.text: Add the mince on high heat, breaking up lumps, 5-6 minutes until no pink remains.

steps.title: Peas
steps.text: Add peas and water. Cover and simmer 10 minutes.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Uncover, add garam masala, reduce until thick. Top with coriander.

recipes.notes: Ask the butcher to mince breast only — mixed mince is much fattier. 4g fibre per serving from the peas and vegetables. Freezes well for 3 months.

recipes.title: Palak Moong Dal

steps.title: Pressure cook
steps.text: Rinse the dal until the water runs clear. Pressure cook with the water, turmeric and half the salt for 2-3 whistles until soft.

steps.title: Tadka
steps.text: Heat ghee, add cumin and garlic until golden, then dried chillies and hing.

steps.title: Onions and tomato
steps.text: Add onion for 4-5 minutes, then tomato and chilli powder for 3 minutes.

steps.title: Spinach
steps.text: Add spinach and let it wilt, about 2 minutes.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Tip in the dal and remaining salt, simmer 5 minutes, adjust water.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Stir in lemon juice.

recipes.notes: 6g fibre per serving — pair it with any of the low-fibre chicken dishes to fix the gap in one go.

recipes.title: Egg White Veggie Bhurji

steps.title: Whisk
steps.text: Whisk eggs and whites with turmeric and salt.

steps.title: Vegetables
steps.text: Heat oil, cook onion 3 minutes, then chilli and capsicum 2 minutes.

steps.title: Tomato
steps.text: Add tomato and chilli powder, cook 2 minutes until soft. Wilt the spinach in for 30 seconds.

steps.title: Eggs
steps.text: Lower the heat, pour in the eggs and stir gently until just set in soft curds. Don't let them dry out.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Garam masala and coriander.

recipes.notes: Regular bhurji runs ~175 kcal per 100g; this is ~125 with roughly twice the protein density.

recipes.title: Sprouts & Chana Chaat

steps.title: Steam
steps.text: Steam the sprouts 3-4 minutes, or use raw if very fresh.

steps.title: Combine
steps.text: Mix the sprouts, chana and vegetables.

steps.title: Dress
steps.text: Add lemon, spices and salt right before eating — salt draws water out of the cucumber.

recipes.notes: 10g fibre in one bowl — the single easiest fix for your fibre gap, and a far better answer to evening hunger than cashews. Keep boiled chana in the fridge (3-4 days) and this takes 3 minutes.

recipes.title: Kachumber Salad

steps.title: Dice
steps.text: Dice everything evenly small, about 1cm.

steps.title: Dress
steps.text: Combine and dress just before serving.

recipes.notes: The default side for any chicken dish in this collection. ~45 kcal for a proper bowl.

recipes.title: Chicken Tikka Wrap

ingredients.name: Air Fryer Tandoori Chicken Tikka (about 170g cooked)
garlic yogurt dip or mint curd chutney

steps.title: Warm
steps.text: Warm the tortilla on a dry tawa, 20-30 seconds per side.

steps.title: Build
steps.text: Spread the dip, add cabbage and onion, then the tikka. Sprinkle chaat masala and lemon.

steps.title: Roll and seal
steps.text: Roll tight, fold the bottom, and toast seam-side down 1 minute.

recipes.notes: Uses one serving of the tandoori tikka recipe — make a batch and this becomes a 5-minute lunch. Uses the tortillas you already buy.

recipes.title: Soya Chunk Masala

steps.title: Boil the soya
steps.text: Boil the chunks in salted water 8-10 minutes.

steps.title: Squeeze
steps.text: Drain, rinse in cold water, and squeeze out ALL the water. This is what stops it tasting of soya.

steps.title: Onions
steps.text: Heat oil, add cumin, then onions for 8 minutes until golden.

steps.title: Masala
steps.text: Add ginger-garlic paste for 1 minute, then tomato puree and powders for 6-7 minutes until oil separates.

steps.title: Fry the soya
steps.text: Add the soya and fry 3-4 minutes so it absorbs the masala.

steps.title: Simmer
steps.text: Add water, cover and simmer 8 minutes.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Garam masala, crushed kasuri methi, coriander.

recipes.notes: The cheapest protein per rupee you can cook, with 7g fibre per serving.

recipes.title: Air Fryer Paneer Tikka

steps.title: Marinate
steps.text: Mix everything except the paneer and vegetables. Coat paneer and veg gently, rest 30 minutes.

steps.title: Preheat
steps.text: Air fryer at 200°C.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: 8 minutes, turn, then 4-5 more until charred at the edges.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Chaat masala over the top.

recipes.notes: Regular paneer adds ~80 kcal and 11g fat per serving. Handle gently — paneer breaks if you stir hard.

recipes.title: Light Kerala Fish Curry

ingredients.name: fish (seer, rohu or basa), steaks or chunks

steps.title: Prep the fish
steps.text: Rub with a pinch of turmeric and salt, rest 10 minutes.

steps.title: Temper
steps.text: Heat coconut oil, crackle the mustard seeds, add curry leaves.

steps.title: Shallots
steps.text: Cook shallots 5 minutes until soft, then ginger-garlic paste and chillies for 1 minute.

steps.title: Spices
steps.text: Lower the heat, add the powders for 30 seconds with a splash of water so they don't burn, then the tomato for 3 minutes.

steps.title: Gravy
steps.text: Add water and kokum, boil 5 minutes.

steps.title: Fish
steps.text: Slide the fish in and simmer gently, uncovered, 8-10 minutes. Swirl the pan instead of stirring.

steps.title: Coconut milk
steps.text: Lower the heat, add coconut milk and warm 2 minutes. Don't boil it — it splits.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Rest 15 minutes before serving. Even better the next day.

recipes.notes: Light coconut milk keeps this at ~250 kcal; full-fat adds about 60 per serving.
